newsitem.title: MEXICO: WEEKLY MEXICO EXPORT, IMPORT FEEDER CATTLE SUMMARY.
newsitem.headline: WEEKLY MEXICO EXPORT, IMPORT FEEDER CATTLE SUMMARY.

text.p: USDA said Friday that steer calves exported to the United States from Mexico sold 4-5 cents/lb lower than compared to two weeks ago.
Exports for the week were estimated at 5,000 head into Texas and New Mexico states, against 1,752 head last week and 266 head in the same week in 1996.

"Trade moderate to active, demand good. Bulk of supply consisted of steers weighing 300-600 lb. Around 80 percent of cattle crossed were exported through Presidio, Texas. Santa Teresa, New Mexico, will begin crossing Aug 12," USDA said.
Prices for feeder steers weighing 300-400 lb were 97-107 cents/lb, for 400-500 lb they were 87-97 cents/lb.
"Demand for slaughter cows remains good in Mexico," it added. Imports into Mexico of slaughter cattle were estimated to have totaled 4,000 head for the week, it added.
((--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com))
